sonnet.problem: Choice card 6 asks about 38:16 (Judah not realizing who she is). Story card 7, which comes after it, then tells 38:15-16, so the cards go backward. The baker is asked about the verse before 38:15 has been told on a story card.
sonnet.rule: Cards follow the passage in order. A choice card can look back at a verse an earlier card in the same stop told, but never jumps ahead.

sonnet.problem: The wrong answer "She leaves it by the road" is not shown false anywhere in the passage. Verse 19 says only that Tamar removed her veil, not what she did with it. It could also be argued to be right alongside "She takes it off".
sonnet.rule: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

sonnet.problem: The question says Tamar "puts her widow's garments back on", which already implies the veil comes off. That nearly gives the right answer, "She takes it off".
sonnet.rule: A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it, like "rock badgers" for "in the rocks." Ask something else.

sonnet.problem: The right answer begins "So they won't..." while both wrong answers begin "Because...", so it stands out. "Because the goat is worth more to him" is also a nonsensical reason, since Judah has already sent the goat.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

sonnet.problem: The joke puts modern items (wallet, ID, car keys) directly onto Judah, a man in the Bible setting. That blends the comparison with the Bible scene, and the car keys are outside Papa Dorin's world. The comparison should be a separate everyday image, like "You know when you'd rather lose...".
sonnet.rule: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

sonnet.problem: The card re-asks a fact already shown on stop 2 card 3, that Tamar was never given to Shelah (also set up in stop 1 cards 11-12). Judah's admission that he did not give her to Shelah is the same fact, so the answer is effectively given away.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: Story card 13 says "Then that little hand pulls right back in." That gives away the answer to choice card 14, whether the twin with the thread is born first (False).
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
